title: Impact of Medicare Eligibility on Hospital Visits

llm_response.content:
## 1. Identification Strategy
Regression Discontinuity Design (RDD). Medicare eligibility has a sharp cutoff at age 65, creating a natural experiment where individuals just below vs. just above this threshold are comparable except for Medicare access. The key assumption is that there are no other factors that change discontinuously at age 65 affecting hospital visits, and that individuals cannot precisely manipulate their age around the cutoff.

## 2. R Code
```r
# Load required libraries
library(rdrobust)
library(ggplot2)

# Read the data
data <- read.csv("experiments/exp_b/data/s86_data.csv")

# Center the running variable around the cutoff (age 65)
# Since treated=1 when running_var > 0, the cutoff is at 0
data$age_centered <- data$running_var

# Basic RDD estimation using rdrobust
rdd_result <- rdrobust(data$y, data$age_centered, c = 0)
print("=== MAIN RDD RESULTS ===")
print(summary(rdd_result))

# Extract and print the key coefficient
treatment_effect <- rdd_result$coef[1]
se <- rdd_result$se[1]
p_value <- rdd_result$pv[1]

cat("\n=== KEY FINDINGS ===\n")
cat(sprintf("Treatment Effect (Medicare Eligibility): %.4f\n", treatment_effect))
cat(sprintf("Standard Error: %.4f\n", se))
cat(sprintf("P-value: %.4f\n", p_value))
cat(sprintf("95%% Confidence Interval: [%.4f, %.4f]\n", 
            treatment_effect - 1.96*se, treatment_effect + 1.96*se))

# Robustness checks
cat("\n=== ROBUSTNESS CHECKS ===\n")

# 1. Different bandwidth
rdd_half_bw <- rdrobust(data$y, data$age_centered, c = 0, h = rdd_result$bws[1]/2)
cat(sprintf("Half bandwidth estimate: %.4f (SE: %.4f)\n", 
            rdd_half_bw$coef[1], rdd_half_bw$se[1]))

rdd_double_bw <- rdrobust(data$y, data$age_centered, c = 0, h = rdd_result$bws[1]*2)
cat(sprintf("Double bandwidth estimate: %.4f (SE: %.4f)\n", 
            rdd_double_bw$coef[1], rdd_double_bw$se[1]))

# 2. Different polynomial orders
rdd_p2 <- rdrobust(data$y, data$age_centered, c = 0, p = 2)
cat(sprintf("Quadratic polynomial estimate: %.4f (SE: %.4f)\n", 
            rdd_p2$coef[1], rdd_p2$se[1]))

# 3. Check for manipulation around cutoff
manipulation_test <- rddensity(data$age_centered, c = 0)
cat(sprintf("Manipulation test p-value: %.4f\n", manipulation_test$test$p_jk))

# Visualization
p1 <- ggplot(data, aes(x = age_centered, y = y)) +
  geom_point(aes(color = factor(treated)), alpha = 0.6) +
  geom_vline(xintercept = 0, linetype = "dashed", color = "red") +
  geom_smooth(data = subset(data, age_centered < 0), method = "lm", se = TRUE, color = "blue") +
  geom_smooth(data = subset(data, age_centered >= 0), method = "lm", se = TRUE, color = "red") +
  labs(title = "RDD: Medicare Eligibility and Hospital Visits",
       x = "Age (centered at 65)",
       y = "Log Hospital Visits",
       color = "Medicare Eligible") +
  theme_minimal()

print(p1)

# Summary statistics by treatment status
cat("\n=== DESCRIPTIVE STATISTICS ===\n")
cat("Below cutoff (No Medicare):\n")
below_stats <- subset(data, treated == 0)
cat(sprintf("  N: %d, Mean log visits: %.4f, SD: %.4f\n", 
            nrow(below_stats), mean(below_stats$y), sd(below_stats$y)))

cat("Above cutoff (Medicare):\n")
above_stats <- subset(data, treated == 1)
cat(sprintf("  N: %d, Mean log visits: %.4f, SD: %.4f\n", 
            nrow(above_stats), mean(above_stats$y), sd(above_stats$y)))
```

## 3. Expected Findings
I expect a positive coefficient of approximately 0.2-0.4, indicating that Medicare eligibility increases hospital visits by 20-40% (in log terms). This is because Medicare reduces the financial barriers to healthcare access, making hospital visits more affordable for the elderly. The effect should be statistically significant as Medicare substantially changes healthcare incentives at the age-65 threshold.

_ground_truth.identification_strategy: Compare individuals just below and above age 65.
_ground_truth.conclusion_detail: Medicare eligibility at age 65 leads to a reduction in hospital visits.
